author: Javier Martín
title: I'm looking for sponsors for the Humanoid Robots Guide
subtitle: I need your help to give a new boost to the outreach work I do at Integrarobot.
body_markdown:
![Image](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/23833069-a60d-42ad-b5cb-b1569cb3925c_1672x941.png)

The time has come to take a new step in the outreach work I do at **Integrarobot**: after the newsletter, the course and the community, it is time to create the **humanoid robots guide**.

The truth is that I thought I could do this work sooner, but analysis paralysis took its toll. On several occasions I was looking for the best moment to publish it, and it seemed that day never came.

Now is the moment of truth, and we are going all out with the publication of: **Humanoid Robots: the opportunity. A guide to working, founding a company or investing in robotics and Physical AI.**

But before its launch, I would like to count on your collaboration in this work, which is going to require significant dedication, in order to reflect in a single document everything that is happening with robotics and physical AI.

To this end, I encourage you to collaborate with me on this guide in the following ways:

1. Join Integrarobot's paid community, because the guide will be available only to those willing to get more involved in the development of this initiative.
2. If you have a company, you can collaborate as a sponsor of the Guide and thereby gain greater visibility in this sector. You will also have advertising space in this newsletter and in the Linkedin one, with more than 5,000 subscribers between them.

How much does it cost to support the development of the Humanoid Robots Guide?

- **10 euros a month** or 100 euros a year if you collaborate as an individual. In addition to the guide, you will have access to the community meetings and the recorded courses on humanoid robots, robotics and Physical AI.
- **1,000 euros** if you collaborate as a company. You will have a page in the Guide dedicated exclusively to your company, and promotion in one of the Substack and Linkedin newsletters. And 10 community accesses for people in your company.

If you have any questions about all this, I encourage you to write to me at [javier@integrarobot.com](mailto:javier@integrarobot.com) :)

My plan is to publish the guide before the end of the year, and so that you have some idea of what it will be like, here is the introduction:

**People want robots**. This is the main conclusion I have reached in the two years I have been studying robotics, especially humanoid robots. But when someone asks me which robot to buy, my answer is: wait, **it is not yet time to buy, but to invest**. This may frustrate many people, but my reasons may help avoid rushing and obtain better results when the time comes to buy a first robot.

To understand it better, let's look at an example. What is happening now with humanoid robotics is very similar to what happened a little over 10 years ago with electric cars. Specifically, from 2010 battery-powered cars could start to be bought, and if you were one of the early adopters you may have had a Nissan Leaf. But of course, that had little more than 100 kilometres of range, and the experience was probably not entirely satisfactory. What to do then? In hindsight this is easy to say, but since I am convinced something similar is going to happen, I'll take the plunge and tell you. Also in 2010, Tesla shares could start to be bought. If at that moment we had devoted the 30,000 euros a Nissan Leaf cost to buying Tesla shares, in a short time, with the return on the shares, you could have bought a Tesla Model S with three times the Leaf's range.

As I say, it is easy to say now, but knowing that it is impossible to predict the future, I dare say that in the next 2 or 3 years a similar situation is going to arise with robots.

Suppose you now want to buy a humanoid robot, and since the easiest option to buy at the moment is Unitree through its distributors in Spain, we would be talking about a cost, depending on the version chosen, of between 25,000 and 50,000 euros. This bearing in mind that, as you know, these robots still don't have the AI part fully developed, and therefore their functionality in terms of manual dexterity is very limited.

But since we are working with an example, let's stick with these amounts, and the experiment would consist of devoting those 25,000 or 50,000 euros to investing in Tesla shares, with a view to the market launch of its Optimus humanoid robot, or if you don't like Tesla, you also have other options, such as buying the KraneShares Global Hmnd Rbtcs & Physical AI Idx ETF, abbreviated KOID, which, among many other companies, has Unitree in its portfolio.

If you are someone who likes action, this speech may seem somewhat defeatist to you, but don't worry, because in this guide I am going to give you many more options. You are not reading a guide devoted exclusively to investing in robotics; you will also find a lot of valuable material if what you want is to found a company or work in the robotics sector, and even if you are totally determined to buy a humanoid robot now, I am going to explain how to do it and how to start getting the most out of this technology.

---

On Wednesday next week, 30 September, we will have an **Integrarobot community meeting**. You can still sign up if you want to become part of this select group of robotics pioneers.

---

## Off Topic

Today I'm going to stray a little from the topic to share with you two news items that really caught my attention and that, although they have nothing to do with robotics, demonstrate very well the pace of acceleration we are experiencing in technology.

🦠[Pioneer Labs](https://x.com/erika_alden_d/status/2102428491493085524) has announced that it wants to begin the **terraforming of Mars**. With equipment that fits in a single rocket launch, they want to turn Martian soil, water and air into building materials to erect a small city on Mars. To achieve this they will look for the best microorganism on Earth and evolve it so that it is able to obtain its nutrients directly from Martian materials.

🌨️ [Rainmaker](https://x.com/ADoricko/status/2092068222183047560) has managed to produce 19 million gallons of water in Alaska through next-generation **cloud seeding** in 3 hours of operations. It is the first company to verifiably produce precipitation in Alaska. In the future, Rainmaker wants to restore glaciers with artificial snowfall and add more water to the Colorado River and the Great Salt Lake.

items.headline: 🏭 Boston Dynamics has launched inside Hyundai's factory in Georgia the RMAC, a centre where Atlas learns through teleoperation to prepare and sequence parts for assembly.
items.body_markdown: 🏭 [Boston Dynamics](https://www.humanoidsdaily.com/news/boston-dynamics-atlas-rmac-training-center) has launched inside **Hyundai**'s factory in Georgia the RMAC, a centre where Atlas learns through teleoperation to prepare and sequence parts for assembly. The facility will be expanded to a building about ten times larger in 2027.

items.headline: 👁️ Cognex will buy RealSense for approximately 500 million dollars in cash, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
items.body_markdown: 👁️ [Cognex](https://www.cognex.com/en/company/press-releases/cognex-to-acquire-realsense) will buy RealSense for approximately **500 million dollars** in cash, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions. This deal unites 2D and 3D industrial vision with depth cameras and robotic navigation.

items.headline: 🧠 SoftBank has reportedly reached an agreement to buy from Hyundai the RAI research institute founded by Marc Raibert.
items.body_markdown: 🧠 [SoftBank](https://www.therobotreport.com/softbank-agrees-to-acquire-robotics-and-ai-institute) has reportedly reached an agreement to buy from Hyundai the RAI research institute founded by Marc Raibert. If completed, SoftBank would add research in learning, manipulation and control to the industrial platform it seeks to build around ABB Robotics and other portfolio companies.

items.headline: 💰 D-Robotics has closed a 400 million dollar Series C to expand its Sunrise chip family and a software platform covering the complete development of the robot.
items.body_markdown: 💰 [D-Robotics](https://en.d-robotics.cc/blog/d-robotics-completes-400-million-in-series-c-funding-driving-the-robotics-industry-into-a-boom-in-product-categories) has closed a **400 million dollar Series C** to expand its Sunrise chip family and a software platform covering the complete development of the robot. The company claims to have surpassed eight million cumulative chips and that its S600 has already been adopted by more than twenty embodied AI customers..

items.headline: 🖥️ Watney has raised 80 million dollars in a Series A, exceeding 100 million in total funding, to deploy robots specialized in the physical work required to build and operate da…
items.body_markdown: 🖥️ [Watney](https://watney.com/media/introducing-watney) has raised **80 million dollars** in a Series A, exceeding 100 million in total funding, to deploy robots specialized in the physical work required to build and operate data centres. The company says it has accumulated hundreds of thousands of hours in customer facilities and more than 99.99% reliability.

items.headline: 🖐️ Unitree presents the Dex5-S dexterous hand, with 22 degrees of freedom, a size similar to a human hand and a price from 6,500 dollars.
items.body_markdown: 🖐️ [Unitree](https://x.com/UnitreeRobotics/status/2101996861259395234) presents the **Dex5-S dexterous hand**, with 22 degrees of freedom, a size similar to a human hand and a price from 6,500 dollars. All its axes support backdrivable movement and torque protection against impacts. This launch makes a critical component cheaper to access so that labs and developers can experiment with dexterity.

items.headline: ⚙️ Core Matter maps who manufactures motors, reducers, screws, encoders, bearings, electronics and materials for humanoid actuators.
items.body_markdown: ⚙️ [Core Matter](https://read.corematter.com/p/humanoid-robot-actuator-suppliers) maps who manufactures motors, reducers, screws, encoders, bearings, electronics and materials for humanoid actuators. Its conclusion is that the bottleneck is not measured only by price: what matters is how many qualified parts each supplier can deliver with consistent precision and quality.

items.headline: 🧪 Midcentury closes a 15 million dollar seed round and a proposal that unites real data and simulation for physical AI.
items.body_markdown: 🧪 [Midcentury](https://x.com/MidcenturyAI/status/2102412610071339414) closes a **15 million dollar seed round** and a proposal that unites real data and simulation for physical AI. It claims to have more than two million hours of egocentric video, 50 environments and 20,000 tasks, as well as Matrix for evaluating and post-training policies at scale.

items.headline: 📉 Eidon AI shuts down after more than two years collecting data for robotics and releases as open code and data its glove, its trackers, its simulator and its video and motion d…
items.body_markdown: 📉 [Eidon AI](https://x.com/theSamPadilla/status/2102533979291443495) shuts down after more than two years collecting data for robotics and releases as open code and data its glove, its trackers, its simulator and its video and motion datasets. Its founder describes a difficult economy: few buyers, incompatible requirements, expensive logistics and quality control, and demand for recurring flows of thousands of hours; it is a valuable reminder that a technical bottleneck does not by itself create a good business.
